subject: URGENT: EmberCare production latency + 5xx in us-west — request for immediate reroute
messages:
From: Mark Turner <mark.turner@embercare.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 27 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: URGENT: Production errors & latency (us-west)

Vanessa —

We started seeing a spike of 5xx errors and request latency from our production traffic routed to us-west-2 around 08:45 PDT. Error rate climbed to ~8% and p95 latency went from ~220ms to 1.8s. This is impacting our checkout flow (payment tokenization).

Attached is a short trace + two screenshots (error_screenshot.png). We're calling Redwood via the standard API endpoint (model pinned to redwood-v2-large) from several customer regions; the impact looks localized to us-west.

Can you please initiate an immediate cross-region reroute to us-east-1 (or another healthy region) and confirm the timeline? We need an ETA within 30 minutes and a plan for rollback/verification. Our execs are on the line.

Sofia and I are available on the phone.

—Mark
Mark Turner
Head of Platform, EmberCare
mark.turner@embercare.com
+1 415-555-0192

Mark / Sofia — thanks for the heads up and the screenshots. I’m escalating and standing this up as an incident.

Immediate plan (high level):
- Looping in Aditya (SE) + Sean (Ops) to validate and execute a geo-redispatch canary to us-east-1.
- We’ll enable prefix/KV cache preservation where possible, route 10% traffic first for verification, then ramp to 100% if green.
- We’ll post a clear rollback point and a post-incident summary.

I’ll also escalate to my leadership for executive visibility; Laura Bennett will be on the thread as well. Standby for timeline from Aditya/Sean — targeting < 30 minutes for the canary.

Vanessa Ortiz

Subject: Re: URGENT: Production errors & latency (us-west) — proposed mitigation steps

Vanessa / Sean / Mark — quick tech note from SE: I pulled the customer trace (thanks Mark) and the error is concentrated on our us-west GPU pool. Likely a transient kernel saturation combined with a model KV-cache thrash after a burst of long sequences.

Proposed immediate steps (will execute pending Sean’s go):
1) Start canary reroute: route 10% of EmberCare prod traffic to us-east-1 (latency tradeoff acceptable per SLA).
2) Use the compatible model variant redwood-v2-large-quant for the canary to reduce memory pressure.
3) Enable prefix caching on the us-east path to minimize cold-kv overhead.
4) Collect per-route token latency + 5xx counts, verify 15m windows before ramp.
5) If canary < 1% errors and p95 < 450ms, ramp 10->50->100 over 20 minutes.

I’ve attached a condensed runbook (runbook_geo_failover.pdf) and a diagnostic bundle (customer_logs.zip). If Ops requests, we can also open a dedicated infra bridge and pin a reserve pool for EmberCare.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: URGENT: EmberCare production latency + 5xx in us-west — executing canary

Team — I’m on it. Actions taken:
- Opened infra bridge INC-20280727-EMB-USW (internal).
- Applied geo-redispatch policy to EmberCare routing rule (10% to us-east-1).
- Deployed redwood-v2-large-quant variant into us-east reserve pool and preserved KV cache snapshot.
- Started telemetry collection (per-route token timing + 5xx).

Early telemetry (5 minutes): canary 10% shows 0.6% 5xx and p95 ~420ms. Continuing observation. If we stay <1% 5xx for two consecutive 15m windows we will proceed to ramp to 50%.

I’ll keep the bridge open and post updates. If Mark/Sofia see any user-facing regressions, flag immediately and we’ll rollback.

—Sean

Mark / Sofia — quick executive update:

What we did:
- Executed a canary reroute (10% -> us-east-1) at 09:40 PDT; telemetry is good (see Sean’s note).
- Laid in the quantized variant to reduce memory pressure and preserve cache snapshots.
- Infra bridge open and diagnostics uploaded to the ticket.

Next steps / ETA:
- Ramp to 50% if next 15m window stays under 1% errors. Full cutover target ~ 30–40 minutes from now assuming steady telemetry.
- If anything regresses we will rollback to us-west and keep you posted.

Executive support: I’ve looped in Laura Bennett (VP Sales) for visibility. We will proactively offer a service credit for the affected window; I’ll coordinate the exact credit amount with Finance/Sales after the incident.

Phone: I’m on standby for the next 45 minutes — feel free to call. Apologies for the disruption; we’ll follow up with a full RCA and action items.
